lessons.title: What Power Query is and what works on Mac
Import a CSV and clean it
learn: Remove columns, change types, filter rows
lessons.mac:
• Data > Get Data (Power Query) > Text/CSV
• First import: click Grant Access when macOS asks for the folder
• Same Applied Steps and commands as on Windows
• Right-click = Control-click (or two-finger tap)
• Refresh All: Data > Refresh All

steps.say: Every month the Pune branch sends a raw sales export as a CSV file. By the end of this lesson, one Power Query will turn it into a clean table of twenty-six invoices, with real dates and product codes that keep their leading zeros. Next month, you only press Refresh.

acts.t:
Finished result

• Sheet S13-02, cell A1: a clean query table of 26 invoices
• Product Code stays text (0733, not 733)
• Inv Date is a real date (English India)
• No Remarks column, no cancelled invoices, no blank rows
• Every step is saved: Data > Refresh All repeats it next month

steps.say: You will learn three things: how to bring a CSV into Power Query, how to remove columns, set data types and filter rows, and how to load the result exactly where you want it. We are on sheet S13-02, and the file is in the data folder next to the workbook.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Import a CSV with Get Data
2. Remove columns, set data types, filter rows
3. Close & Load To a chosen cell

Practice: sheet S13-02 · file data/Pune_Sales_Apr-2026.csv

steps.say: Think of Power Query as a recorder for cleaning. It reads the source, you click through the fixes, and each fix is saved as an applied step. Your original CSV is never changed, and refreshing runs every step again on the new data.

acts.t:
How Power Query works

Source file  →  Applied Steps  →  Close & Load

• Source: the CSV, untouched
• Applied Steps: each cleaning action, in order, editable
• Close & Load: puts the result in a table in Excel
• Refresh: runs all steps again on new data

steps.say: Go to sheet S13-02 and click cell A1. On the Data tab, click Get Data, then From File, then From Text slash CSV. On a Mac, the same button is called Get Data, Power Query, and you pick Text slash CSV.
Choose the file Pune Sales April 2026 from the data folder and click Import.
Excel shows a preview. Don't click Load yet. Click Transform Data to open the Power Query editor, where the cleaning happens.

Look at the Product Code column. The code zero seven three three now shows as seven hundred and thirty-three. Power Query guessed the column was a number and dropped the leading zero. That guess is the Changed Type step in the Applied Steps list.
Click Changed Type in Applied Steps and press Delete. Every column goes back to text, and we will set the types ourselves. Never trust automatic types for codes, PIN codes or phone numbers.
Click the Remarks header. It only has notes like call back, so on the Home tab click Remove Columns. A new step called Removed Columns appears on the right.
Now the number columns. Click the Qty header, open Data Type and choose Whole Number. Do the same for Rate and Amount. Leave Product Code as text, so zero seven three three stays exactly as it is.

The dates are written day, month, year. Right-click the Inv Date header, choose Change Type, then Using Locale. Set Data Type to Date and Locale to English India, and click OK. This works whatever region your Mac is set to.
Next, the cancelled invoices. Open the filter arrow on the Status header, untick Cancelled and click OK. Four invoices drop out of the preview.
The export also has one empty line in the middle. On the Home tab, click Remove Rows, then Remove Blank Rows. Notice the list of applied steps reads like a checklist of what we did.
Click the arrow under Close and Load, and choose Close and Load To. Pick Table, then Existing worksheet, cell A1 on sheet S13-02, and click OK.
The clean table lands at A1. The counter in L2 shows twenty-six rows, and the total in L5 is six lakh eighty-seven thousand two hundred and thirty rupees. Product codes still start with zero.

Next month, save May's export with the same file name and click Refresh All on the Data tab. Every step runs again in seconds. If the file name changes, use Data Source Settings to point the query at the new file.

A few Mac differences. The button is Get Data, Power Query. The first time, macOS asks you to grant access to the folder, so allow it. The Mac editor looks like the web version, but the step names and ribbon commands are the same. Right-click is Control-click.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Data > Get Data (Power Query) > Text/CSV
• First import: click Grant Access when macOS asks for the folder
• Same Applied Steps and commands as on Windows
• Right-click = Control-click (or two-finger tap)
• Refresh All: Data > Refresh All

steps.say: To recap: import through Get Data and always choose Transform Data. Set your own data types, using a locale for Indian dates. And load to a fixed cell so your formulas can find the table.

acts.t:
Recap

• Get Data > Text/CSV > Transform Data
• Delete guessed types; set them yourself (Using Locale for DD-MM-YYYY)
• Close & Load To a fixed cell, then Refresh All next month

steps.say: Your challenge: edit the query so that only Pending invoices load. How many rows do you get, and what is the total? The answer is at the bottom of the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Double-click the query in Queries & Connections and change the Status filter to Pending only.
How many rows load, and what is the total in L5?

Answer: bottom of sheet S13-02 Done

lessons.title: Split, replace, fill down and add columns
lessons.mac:
• Data > From Table/Range opens the same editor
• Column From Examples: recent Microsoft 365 builds only
• No Column From Examples? Add Column > Extract > Range, start 2, length 10 (Power Query counts from 0)

steps.say: This customer master came from an old system. Name and city share one column, the region is typed only once per group, and active status is just Y or N. We will turn it into a clean list with a PAN column and a credit band, all in Power Query.

acts.t:
Finished result

• Query table at S13-03!H1, 16 customers
• Customer and City in separate columns
• Region filled down for every row
• Active / Inactive instead of Y / N
• PAN taken from the GSTIN (Column From Examples)
• Credit Band: High if limit ≥ ₹5,00,000, else Standard

steps.say: You will learn to split a column, replace values, fill down blanks, and add new columns two ways: by example and by a condition. The practice table is tblCustomers on sheet S13-03.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Split Column by delimiter, then Trim
2. Replace Values and Fill Down
3. Column From Examples and Conditional Column

Practice: sheet S13-03, table tblCustomers

steps.say: Here is a quick map of the commands. Split and Replace are on the Home tab. Fill Down and Trim are on the Transform tab. New columns live on the Add Column tab, which never changes the original column.

acts.t:
Where the commands live

Home tab: Split Column, Replace Values
Transform tab: Fill > Down, Format > Trim, Rename
Add Column tab: Column From Examples, Conditional Column

Transform changes a column. Add Column creates a new one.

steps.say: Click any cell in the table, say A2. On the Data tab, click From Table slash Range. The editor opens with the table already loaded.
Click the header Customer, City. On the Home tab, choose Split Column, By Delimiter. Choose Comma, split at the left-most delimiter, and click OK.

acts.h: Set Select or enter delimiter to Comma

steps.say: Two columns appear, but look closely at the city. It starts with a space, left over from after the comma. Spaces like this make lookups fail later, so it is a mistake worth catching now.
Click the second column, go to the Transform tab, open Format and choose Trim. Then use Rename on the same tab to call the columns Customer and City.
Now the Region column. It says West once, then nulls until North. Click the Region header, and on the Transform tab choose Fill, then Down. Every row now carries its region.
Click the Active header. On the Home tab click Replace Values. Value to find, capital Y. Replace with, Active. Click OK, then repeat with capital N and Inactive.
A GSTIN has the PAN inside it, from the third to the twelfth character. Click the GSTIN header, then on the Add Column tab choose Column From Examples, From Selection.
In the first empty cell, type the PAN for Sharma Traders, A A A C S one two three four F, and press Enter. Power Query works out the rule and fills every row. Rename the column to PAN and click OK.
Last, a credit band. On the Add Column tab click Conditional Column. Name it Credit Band. If Credit Limit is greater than or equal to five lakh, the output is High. Else, Standard. Click OK.

acts.h: Set New column name to Credit Band
Set Operator to is greater than or equal to

steps.say: Choose Close and Load To, Existing worksheet, cell H1 on this sheet, and click OK. The clean list sits beside the original, and both stay in step whenever you refresh.
Prove it is repeatable. In cell D4, change Desai Pharma from N to Y, then click Refresh All. In the output, Desai Pharma flips to Active. Change it back to N and refresh again.

On a Mac, From Table slash Range is on the Data tab as well. Column From Examples needs a recent Microsoft 365 build; if you don't see it, use Extract, Range on the Transform tab with a start of two and a length of ten.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Data > From Table/Range opens the same editor
• Column From Examples: recent Microsoft 365 builds only
• No Column From Examples? Add Column > Extract > Range, start 2, length 10 (Power Query counts from 0)

steps.say: To recap: split on a delimiter and trim the spaces. Fill down blanks and replace codes with words. Add new columns by example or by a rule, on the Add Column tab.

acts.t:
Recap

• Split Column + Trim = clean text
• Fill Down and Replace Values fix exports from old systems
• Column From Examples and Conditional Column add logic without formulas

steps.say: Your challenge: add a State Code column with the first two characters of the GSTIN. Sharma Traders should show twenty-seven, the code for Maharashtra. The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Add a State Code column: the first 2 characters of GSTIN
(Add Column > Extract > First Characters).
Sharma Traders should show 27 (Maharashtra).

Answer: bottom of sheet S13-03 Done

lessons.title: Unpivot and pivot
lessons.mac:
• Transform > Unpivot Columns > Unpivot Other Columns
• Select several headers: ⌘ + click (Shift + click for a run)
• Pivot Column is on the same tab

steps.say: Budgets usually arrive like this: one column per month. That looks fine on paper but makes PivotTables and charts painful. We will reshape it into a tall table with one row per region, category and month, a hundred and forty-four rows in all.

acts.t:
Finished result

• New sheet with a query table: Region | Category | Month | Sales
• 144 rows (12 region-category pairs × 12 months)
• Ready for PivotTables, SUMIFS and charts
• Bonus: Pivot Column turns it back into a wide table

steps.say: You will learn to unpivot month columns into rows, why tall data is easier to analyse, and how to pivot it back when a report needs it. The practice table is tblBudget on sheet S13-04.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Unpivot Other Columns
2. Why tall (unpivoted) data is easier
3. Pivot Column, the reverse

Practice: sheet S13-04, table tblBudget

steps.say: Here is the idea. A wide table puts a value in every month column. A tall table has a single Month column and a single Sales column. Unpivot moves from wide to tall. Pivot goes back.

acts.t:
Wide vs tall

Wide: Region | Category | Apr | May | Jun | … | Mar
Tall:  Region | Category | Month | Sales

Unpivot: wide → tall (columns become rows)
Pivot: tall → wide (row values become columns)

Tip: select the columns to KEEP, then Unpivot Other Columns.

steps.say: Click cell A2 in the budget table. On the Data tab, click From Table slash Range.

A common mistake is to select all twelve month columns and choose Unpivot Columns. It works today, but if next year's file adds a column, the new column is left out. So select the columns you want to keep instead.
Click the Region header, then hold Shift and press the right arrow, so Region and Category are both selected. On the Transform tab, open Unpivot Columns and choose Unpivot Other Columns.
Twelve rows became a hundred and forty-four. Power Query named the new columns Attribute and Value. Click Attribute and rename it to Month, then rename Value to Sales.

Why is this better? With one Sales column, a PivotTable can total by month, by region or by category with a single drag, and SUMIFS needs only one sum range. Adding a new month adds rows, not columns.
Now the reverse. Click the Category header. On the Transform tab click Pivot Column. Choose Sales as the values column, keep Sum, and click OK. Each category becomes its own column again.
That view is handy for a printed report, but we want the tall table for analysis. Click the Pivoted Column step and press Delete to remove it. Steps are easy to undo this way.
On the Home tab, click Close and Load. The tall table lands on a new sheet named after the query.
Pro tip: the Month column is text, so Apr to Mar won't sort in order on its own. Add a Month Number column with a Conditional Column or a small lookup table, and sort by it in your PivotTable.

acts.t:
Pro tip

Month names sort alphabetically (Apr, Aug, Dec…).
Add a Month No. column (Apr = 1 … Mar = 12 for the April-March year) and sort by it.

steps.say: On a Mac, Unpivot Columns and Pivot Column are on the Transform tab of the Mac editor too. To select several columns, hold Command and click each header.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Transform > Unpivot Columns > Unpivot Other Columns
• Select several headers: ⌘ + click (Shift + click for a run)
• Pivot Column is on the same tab

steps.say: To recap: keep the identifier columns and unpivot the others. Tall data feeds PivotTables, charts and SUMIFS with less effort. Pivot Column brings back the wide view when a report needs it.

acts.t:
Recap

• Select columns to keep → Unpivot Other Columns
• Tall data = one value column, easy to analyse
• Pivot Column reverses it; delete a step to undo

steps.say: Your challenge: open the query again and use Group By on Region to total Sales for the whole year. Which region has the highest budget? The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

Edit the query: Home > Group By, group by Region, Sum of Sales.
Which region has the highest FY 2026-27 budget?

Answer: bottom of sheet S13-04 Done

lessons.title: Append and merge queries
learn: Join sales to a product master
lessons.mac:
• Open the editor: Data > Queries & Connections, double-click a query
• Home > Append Queries / Merge Queries work the same
• Select the key column in each preview before clicking OK

steps.say: Three branches, Mumbai, Delhi and Bengaluru, each keep their own sales sheet with only product codes. We will stack them into one table and bring in the product name, category and GST rate from the product master.

acts.t:
Finished result

• Query table at S13-05!A12: 24 sales rows from 3 branches
• Columns: Date | Branch | Product Code | Qty | Amount | Product Name | Category | GST Rate
• J13 counts 24 rows; J16 totals ₹6,45,030
• Add a branch or a product later and Refresh All

steps.say: You will learn two ideas. Append stacks tables with the same columns, one under the other. Merge joins two tables side by side on a matching column, like XLOOKUP. Everything is on sheet S13-05.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Load tables as connections only
2. Append Queries (stack rows)
3. Merge Queries (join columns), then Expand

Practice: sheet S13-05, tables tblMumbai, tblDelhi, tblBengaluru, tblProducts

steps.say: Append adds rows, so the column names must match. Merge adds columns, using a key such as Product Code. Left Outer keeps every sales row, even if a code is missing from the master.

acts.t:
Append vs Merge

Append = stack rows (same column names)
Mumbai + Delhi + Bengaluru → one sales list

Merge = join columns on a key (like XLOOKUP)
Sales[Product Code] ↔ tblProducts[Product Code]
Join kind: Left Outer = keep all sales rows

steps.say: First, each table becomes a query that only holds a connection. Click A2 in the Mumbai table, choose From Table slash Range, then Close and Load To, Only Create Connection, OK.
Repeat the same steps for the Delhi table, the Bengaluru table and the product master. Connection-only queries don't add sheets, so the workbook stays tidy.
Open the editor again with Get Data, Launch Power Query Editor. In the Queries list on the left, click tblMumbai.
On the Home tab, open Append Queries and choose Append Queries as New. Pick Three or more tables. Add tblDelhi and tblBengaluru to the list on the right, and click OK.
A new query called Append1 holds all twenty-four rows. The Date column shows a time as well, so click the Date header, open Data Type and choose Date.

Now the lookup. On the Home tab, open Merge Queries and choose Merge Queries. In the top preview, click the Product Code column. Choose tblProducts as the second table and click its Product Code column. Keep Left Outer and click OK.

acts.h: Set Join Kind to Left Outer (all from first, matching from second)

steps.say: A new column called tblProducts shows the word Table in each row. That is a mistake beginners stop at: the data is still folded inside. Click the column, then on the Transform tab choose Expand.
Untick Product Code, because we already have it, and untick Use original column name as prefix. Click OK. Product Name, Category and GST Rate are now in every row.

acts.h: Untick Use original column name as prefix

steps.say: Choose Close and Load To, Table, Existing worksheet, cell A12 on sheet S13-05, and click OK.
The combined table starts at A12. J13 counts twenty-four rows and J16 totals six lakh forty-five thousand and thirty rupees, which matches the three branch tables added together.
Pro tip: when a fourth branch opens, give its table the same columns, load it as a connection, and add it to the Append step. Every report built on this query picks it up on the next refresh.

acts.t:
Pro tip

New branch? Same column names → load as connection → add it in the Append step (gear icon next to Source).
New product? Add a row to tblProducts → Refresh All.

steps.say: On a Mac, there is no Launch Power Query Editor button on some builds. Open Queries and Connections on the Data tab and double-click any query instead. Append Queries and Merge Queries are on the editor's Home tab, as here.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Open the editor: Data > Queries & Connections, double-click a query
• Home > Append Queries / Merge Queries work the same
• Select the key column in each preview before clicking OK

steps.say: To recap: append stacks tables that share column names. Merge joins on a key, like a lookup. After a merge, always expand the new column to get the fields you need.

acts.t:
Recap

• Connection-only queries keep the workbook clean
• Append = rows; Merge = columns on a key
• Expand the merged column, untick the prefix

steps.say: Your challenge: add a custom column called GST Amount equal to Amount multiplied by GST Rate, and find the total GST for all three branches. The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

In Append1: Add Column > Custom Column
GST Amount = [Amount] * [GST Rate]
What is the total GST?

Answer: bottom of sheet S13-05 Done

lessons.title: Combine a folder of monthly files
learn: Tally or bank exports dropped in a folder
lessons.mac:
• Data > Get Data (Power Query) > Folder (recent Microsoft 365 builds)
• Allow folder access when macOS asks
• Not available on your build? Build it once on the web or Windows; refresh works on Mac

steps.say: Our accountant exports the Day Book from Tally every month and drops it in one folder. Each file has title rows on top and a Grand Total row at the bottom. We will combine April, May and June into one clean ledger, and July will just need a refresh.

acts.t:
Finished result

• Sheet S13-06, cell A1: one table from every CSV in data/Monthly_Ledger
• Columns: Month | Date | Particulars | Vch Type | Vch No. | Debit | Credit
• 42 vouchers (Apr-Jun); J5 Debit ₹36,15,500; J8 Credit ₹12,20,000
• Title rows and Grand Total rows removed from every file
• Next month: drop the file in the folder, Refresh All

steps.say: You will learn to combine every file in a folder, to clean the sample file so the fix applies to all files, and to repair the error this usually causes. Practice sheet S13-06, folder data, Monthly Ledger.

acts.t:
In this lesson

1. Get Data > From Folder > Combine & Transform
2. Clean the Transform Sample File once, for all files
3. Fix the Changed Type error, add the Month column

Practice: sheet S13-06 · folder data/Monthly_Ledger

steps.say: Here is how folder combining works. Power Query builds a helper called Transform Sample File from the first file. Whatever you do to that sample runs on every file, and the results are stacked with the file name in front.

acts.t:
How From Folder works

Folder → list of files
        ↓
Transform Sample File (your cleaning, done once)
        ↓
Applied to every file, then stacked
+ Source.Name column = which file each row came from

steps.say: Go to sheet S13-06 and click A1. On the Data tab, choose Get Data, From File, From Folder.
Paste the path of the Monthly Ledger folder and click OK. Power Query lists the three files. Open the Combine button and choose Combine and Transform Data.
The Combine Files window previews the first file. You can see the company name, the words Day Book and the date range above the real headings. Click OK; we will clean them in the sample.
In the Queries list, click Transform Sample File. On the Home tab, choose Remove Rows, Remove Top Rows, type four and click OK. Then click Use First Row as Headers.
Every Tally file ends with a Grand Total line, which would double our totals. Choose Remove Rows, Remove Bottom Rows, type one and click OK.

Now click the main query, Monthly Ledger. You will see an error: the column Column1 was not found. This is the most common folder mistake. The main query's Changed Type step still uses the old column names.
The fix is simple. Click the last step, Changed Type, and press Delete. The data appears with the proper headings, from all three files.

The first column, Source dot Name, holds file names like Ledger underscore Apr dash 2026 dot csv. Click it and use Replace Values twice: replace Ledger underscore with nothing, then dot csv with nothing.
Rename Source dot Name to Month. Then set Debit and Credit to Decimal Number, so the blanks become nulls and the totals add up.
Choose Close and Load To, Table, Existing worksheet, cell A1 on sheet S13-06, and click OK.
Forty-two vouchers from three months. Total debit is thirty-six lakh fifteen thousand five hundred rupees, and total credit is twelve lakh twenty thousand. No Grand Total rows sneaked in.
Next month, copy the July file from the Next Month folder into Monthly Ledger and click Refresh All. The row count goes from forty-two to fifty-four, with no other work.

acts.t:
Next month

1. Copy data/Next_Month/Ledger_Jul-2026.csv into data/Monthly_Ledger
2. Data > Refresh All
3. Rows loaded: 42 → 54

Keep only same-format files in the folder. A stray PDF or Excel file will break the combine.

steps.say: On a Mac, From Folder is under Get Data, Power Query, if your build supports it. If you don't see it, keep the files on OneDrive and build the query in Excel for the web or on Windows; it still refreshes on the Mac.

acts.t:
Mac corner

• Data > Get Data (Power Query) > Folder (recent Microsoft 365 builds)
• Allow folder access when macOS asks
• Not available on your build? Build it once on the web or Windows; refresh works on Mac

steps.say: To recap: From Folder combines every file in one go. Clean the Transform Sample File, not each file. If the main query shows a column not found error, delete its Changed Type step.

acts.t:
Recap

• Get Data > From Folder > Combine & Transform Data
• Clean once in Transform Sample File
• Column not found? Delete Changed Type in the main query

steps.say: Your challenge: use Group By on Vch Type to total the Debit column. How much was billed as Sales across the three months? The answer is on the Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge

In the query: Home > Group By, group by Vch Type, Sum of Debit.
What is the total Sales debit for April to June?

Answer: bottom of sheet S13-06 Done
